title: Attachment supply record (PROPOSED, DEL-01-04/NIR-v0.2 §6; schema 0.2 at RV21)
description: PROPOSED by DEL-01-04/NIR-v0.2 (R17-1; REQ-003), revised at RV21 for R21-2. The identity of the content the App actually put in a turn for an attachment, taken when the turn input is written (AT-1…AT-9). An attachment is carried in one of three ways (R21-2): a text file as a text element of the turn, with the file named (form 'text-element'); an image as an 'image' or 'localImage' input (forms 'localImage', 'image-url', 'image-fileId'); any other file by naming its path for the agent to read with its tools (form 'path-named'). Only the first two are 'supplied'; the third is 'named; read only if a tool item shows it'. 'mention' and 'skill' are not attachment forms: at Codex 0.158.0 'mention' delivered nothing to the model and 'skill' was honoured only for a discovered SKILL.md at its canonical path (observed, OBS-3 W-3, W-1). Every record is App-observed; whether the provider adopted the content is not observed. 'method' names a content-identity designation only; no algorithm is chosen (RS U-04; HOSTING U-08). Handed to the conversation view, to DEL-02-02 for a draft tried in a conversation (K-7; AT-8), and cited by DEL-04-03 records as an evidence reference of kind 'content identity'. No storage location is chosen (TBD-003; OI-014). CC-NIR-ATTACHMENT-REF candidate2026-10-05: schema shape/ID0.2 unchanged; new App submission references and prepared/carrier standing resolve through named HOSTING client-custodyv0.10 successor after joined review. No new correlation store/RS kind/native payload copy.

attachmentId.description: Owning opaque attachment identity. New reference spelling attachment:<attachmentId> resolves this exact ID under NIR supply custody; refs are not filesystem paths. The ordered HOSTING supplyRefs list resolves immutable records sharing turnRef=submissionRef; uniqueness/order/correspondence are receiver checks.

suppliedAs.description: How the attachment is carried in the turn (R21-2): 'text-element' (a text file: a text element of the turn holding an App-written line naming the file and then the file's bytes, AT-9); 'localImage' (UserInput localImage {path}); 'image-url', 'image-fileId' (UserInput image by url or supplier file id); 'path-named' (any other file: its path named in an App-written text element for the agent to read with its tools, AT-10). 'mention' and 'skill' are not used (OBS-3 W-3, W-1).

enum: named; read only if a tool item shows it
supplyStanding.description: Carrier standing, not standalone dispatch/receipt/adoption evidence. A pre-recorded submission is displayed prepared/not sent until actual native write is observed; crash/reload without reliable write custody remains unknown. Historical sent instances retain their actual evidence.

remoteRef.description: A URL or supplier file identity, recorded as given; the App does not fetch it.

elementIdentity.description: Identity of the complete composed text element (naming line plus exact text bytes, or named-path line). Prepared identity does not establish dispatch; native write and response remain existing HOSTING custody observations.

turnRef.description: CC-NIR-ATTACHMENT-REF named candidate: immutable App-owned submission:<opaque UUID> for a new pre-recorded dispatch, awaiting native correlation through HOSTING v0.10 submissionAssociation; never a guessed native turn ID. Historical observed-turn references retain actual meaning. Full client generation/RPC/method belong to HOSTING, not this field.

enum: not applicable: the bytes are in the turn's own text element
not observed: Codex reads the path itself
not applicable: content passed by reference
not observed: read only if a tool item shows it

toolReads.description: For 'path-named' only: tool items of the conversation that name this path, as the App observed them (for example a command or file read). They show that the agent read the path then; which bytes it read stays not observed.

draft.description: AT-8 (K-7; C-14): the attachment is a draft's file tried in an ordinary conversation. The draft is not a registered workflow and the conversation is not a workflow run.

standing.const: draft — not a registered workflow; this conversation is not a workflow run

enum: changed after it was supplied; what Codex read is not observed

Reference forms carry the reference; the App read no bytes.
